question: What is the difference between a <div> and a <span>?
answer_hints: div is block-level (starts on a new line, takes full width); span is inline (flows with text). Both are non-semantic containers.
follow_ups: When would you avoid using div and reach for a semantic element instead?

question: What does semantic HTML mean? Name five semantic elements and what they're for.
answer_hints: Elements that describe their meaning: header, nav, main, article, section, aside, footer, figure. Benefits: accessibility (screen readers), SEO, readability.
follow_ups: What's the difference between article and section?

question: What is the purpose of the alt attribute on images? What happens if it's empty vs missing?
answer_hints: Text alternative for screen readers and when image fails to load. alt="" marks image as decorative (skipped by screen readers); missing alt makes readers announce the filename.
follow_ups: How would you write alt text for a chart or graph?

question: How would you build a form with a required email field and a submit button that validates without any JavaScript?
answer_hints: input type="email" with required attribute; browser handles validation on submit. Mention pattern, minlength, novalidate to disable.
follow_ups: How do you style an invalid field with CSS only? (:invalid, :user-invalid)

question: What's the difference between id and class attributes?
answer_hints: id must be unique per page, used for anchors, label/for, aria references; class is reusable for styling groups. id has higher CSS specificity.
follow_ups: Why is styling by id generally discouraged?

question: What does the DOCTYPE declaration do? What happens without it?
answer_hints: Tells the browser to use standards mode. Without it: quirks mode — legacy box model, inconsistent rendering.
follow_ups: What is quirks mode and can you name one difference it causes?

question: How do you open a link in a new tab safely? What attributes do you need and why?
answer_hints: target="_blank" with rel="noopener noreferrer". noopener prevents the new page accessing window.opener (tab-nabbing); noreferrer also hides the referrer.
follow_ups: Do modern browsers imply noopener for target=_blank?

question: What is the difference between <script>, <script defer> and <script async>?
answer_hints: Plain: blocks parsing, executes immediately. defer: downloads in parallel, executes after parsing in order. async: downloads in parallel, executes as soon as ready (order not guaranteed).
follow_ups: Which would you use for an analytics snippet vs your app bundle?

question: A developer wrote <button> inside an <a> tag and clicks behave strangely. Why is this a problem?
answer_hints: Interactive elements can't be nested — invalid HTML; browsers may reparent them and event behavior becomes unpredictable. Pick one: style a link as a button or handle navigation in the button.
follow_ups: When should something be a link vs a button?

question: What are data-* attributes and when would you use them?
answer_hints: Custom attributes for embedding data on elements, read via element.dataset. Good for hooks/test ids/light state; not a replacement for proper state management.
follow_ups: How do you read data-user-id from JavaScript? (dataset.userId — camelCase)

question: Explain how the browser parses an HTML document into the DOM. What blocks parsing?
answer_hints: Tokenizer → tree construction; parsing is incremental. Synchronous scripts block parsing (may document.write); CSS blocks script execution (scripts can read computed styles). Preload scanner fetches resources ahead.
follow_ups: What is the preload scanner and why does it matter for performance?

question: Build an accessible custom dropdown: what HTML structure and ARIA attributes would you use?
answer_hints: Prefer native <select> first. Custom: button with aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-expanded; list with role="listbox", options with role="option", aria-selected; keyboard support (arrows, Enter, Esc), focus management.
follow_ups: Why is the native select often still the better choice on mobile?

question: What is the difference between localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies? When is each appropriate?
answer_hints: localStorage: persistent, ~5-10MB, per-origin, not sent to server. sessionStorage: per-tab lifetime. Cookies: ~4KB, sent with every request, can be httpOnly/secure — right place for session tokens.
follow_ups: Why should auth tokens generally not live in localStorage?

question: Your marketing team wants a page to rank better and be readable by screen readers, but the page is built entirely of divs with click handlers. What would you change and how would you prioritize?
answer_hints: Look for: semantic landmarks (header/nav/main), real buttons/links (keyboard + SR support for free), heading hierarchy, alt text, form labels. Prioritize interactive elements first (biggest a11y wins), then structure/landmarks.
follow_ups: How would you verify improvements? (Lighthouse, axe, keyboard-only walkthrough, screen reader test)

question: How do you make an image responsive so mobile users don't download a huge desktop image?
answer_hints: srcset with width descriptors + sizes attribute, or <picture> for art direction/format switching (AVIF/WebP with fallback). Mention loading="lazy" and width/height to avoid layout shift.
follow_ups: What's the difference between srcset and the picture element?

question: Explain the difference between the DOM and the HTML you write. Can they differ?
answer_hints: DOM is the live parsed tree; browsers fix invalid markup (auto-close tags, move misplaced elements like table text), and JS mutates it. View-source vs inspector shows the difference.
follow_ups:
Give an example where the browser rewrites your markup (e.g.,

or outside ).

question: A form submits when the user clicks a 'Cancel' button inside it. Why, and how do you fix it?
answer_hints: Buttons inside forms default to type="submit". Fix: type="button". Also mention Enter-key implicit submission behavior.
follow_ups: Which button does Enter trigger when a form has multiple submit buttons? (the first one)

question: What are web components (custom elements, shadow DOM, templates)? What problems do they solve?
answer_hints: Framework-agnostic reusable components: customElements.define, shadow DOM for style/DOM encapsulation, <template>/<slot>. Good for design systems shared across stacks; trade-offs: SSR, styling across shadow boundary.
follow_ups: How does shadow DOM style encapsulation work — what leaks through? (inherited properties, CSS custom properties)

question: How would you implement an accessible modal dialog? Consider focus, keyboard and screen readers.
answer_hints: Prefer native <dialog> with showModal() (focus trap, Esc, ::backdrop, inert background for free). Manual: role="dialog", aria-modal, focus trap, return focus on close, Esc handler, aria-labelledby.
follow_ups: What does the inert attribute do?

question: You need to embed a third-party widget (e.g., a chat bubble) without letting it break or read your page. What are your options?
answer_hints: iframe for isolation (separate origin, sandbox attribute, allow list), postMessage for communication. Script embeds are riskier: global namespace, CSS bleed, security. Mention CSP.
follow_ups: What does the iframe sandbox attribute actually restrict?

question: Walk through what happens in the browser from receiving HTML bytes to pixels on screen (critical rendering path).
answer_hints: Bytes → tokens → DOM; CSS → CSSOM; DOM+CSSOM → render tree; layout (geometry); paint (rasterize layers); composite. Render-blocking CSS, parser-blocking JS, reflow vs repaint vs composite-only (transform/opacity).
follow_ups: Which CSS properties can animate without triggering layout or paint?

question: Design the document structure and loading strategy for a content site that must hit excellent Core Web Vitals on slow devices.
answer_hints: Look for: SSR/static HTML, inline critical CSS, defer JS, priority hints/preload for LCP image, font-display strategy + preload fonts, explicit dimensions to prevent CLS, lazy-load below fold, minimal third parties.
follow_ups: How do you find and prioritize the LCP element?
What commonly causes CLS and how do you prevent each cause?

question: Explain how ARIA live regions work. When do aria-live polite vs assertive apply, and what are common pitfalls?
answer_hints: Announce dynamic changes to screen readers: aria-live="polite" (waits) vs "assertive" (interrupts); role="status"/"alert" shortcuts. Pitfalls: region must exist before content changes, over-announcing, hidden regions.
follow_ups: How would you announce 'Item added to cart' after an AJAX action?

question:
Your page's SSR HTML looks correct, but after hydration the browser shows duplicated or reshuffled content. The markup contains a

wrapping a

. Explain what's happening.
answer_hints:
Invalid nesting: browser's parser closes

before

, so the client-generated DOM doesn't match server HTML → hydration mismatch → React re-creates/moves nodes. Fix the invalid markup.
follow_ups: What other common causes of hydration mismatch have you seen? (dates, random ids, browser extensions)

question: How would you implement an infinitely scrolling accessible list of 100k items without destroying performance?
answer_hints: Virtualization/windowing (render only visible rows), IntersectionObserver for load-more sentinel, content-visibility: auto as a lighter option, stable item heights or measurement, aria-setsize/aria-posinset, focus handling on recycle.
follow_ups: What breaks for accessibility and find-in-page when you virtualize, and how do you mitigate?

question: What is the difference between shadow DOM and iframe isolation? Compare their security and styling boundaries.
answer_hints: Shadow DOM: style/DOM encapsulation only — same JS realm, no security boundary; inherited styles and custom properties cross. iframe: separate browsing context, real origin-based security boundary, own realm; heavier, needs postMessage.
follow_ups: When would you pick each for a design system vs a payment widget?

question: SEO reports your SPA's pages aren't being indexed properly. What do you investigate and what solutions do you propose?
answer_hints: Investigate: what Googlebot sees (rendered vs raw HTML), meta/canonical/robots, status codes for client routes, lazy content requiring interaction. Solutions: SSR/SSG/prerendering, proper titles/meta per route, sitemap, structured data.
follow_ups: How does Google handle JavaScript rendering and why is it still risky to rely on it?

question: Your company needs one header/nav shared across apps built in React, Vue and plain HTML. How would you ship it?
answer_hints: Web component (custom element) is the natural fit: framework-agnostic, shadow DOM for style isolation, attributes/events as API. Discuss SSR limitations, versioning/distribution (CDN vs npm), design tokens via CSS custom properties.
follow_ups: How would the apps communicate auth state to the shared header?

question: A table with 5000 rows makes the whole page janky even when just hovering. The CSS has tr:hover rules and the table is inside a container with box-shadow. How do you diagnose and fix?
answer_hints: DevTools Performance panel: look for large paint areas/layout thrash. Hover triggers repaint of huge layer; shadow makes paints expensive. Fixes: virtualization, content-visibility, simplify hover paint, will-change/containment (contain: paint/layout).
follow_ups: What does CSS contain do and when is it safe?

question: Implement drag-and-drop file upload with a fallback, progress and accessibility. What APIs and markup do you use?
answer_hints: input type="file" (always present — it's the accessible path), dragover/drop events + DataTransfer, FormData + fetch/XHR for progress events, aria-live for status announcements, validate type/size client- and server-side.
follow_ups: Why does fetch make upload progress hard, and what do you use instead? (XHR upload.onprogress or streams)
